name: fraud-detector
intended_use: This model is a fraud detector for credit card transactions, designed to flag potentially fraudulent payments in real-time for automated review or blocking. The intended consumers are the transaction authorization pipeline and the fraud operations team who review flagged transactions.
training_data: Trained on the card_activity feature group from Week 4 (card_activity_features_v1), which contains aggregated transaction history, merchant category encodings, and amount statistics per card. Coverage spans 6 months of historical transactions; known limits include no behavioral features for new cards (<30 days history) and no geographic/IP signals.
limitations: As a simple amount-threshold classifier, this model structurally cannot catch fraud that mimics typical transaction amounts (e.g., low-value card testing, or high-value transactions consistent with the cardholder's history). It has no concept of velocity, location anomaly, or merchant risk — any fraud pattern not correlated with transaction amount will be missed.
ethical_considerations: A false positive (legitimate transaction blocked) directly inconveniences the cardholder, risks reputational damage, and may cause financial harm if the card is their only payment method. A false negative (fraud that gets through) transfers financial loss to the issuer or merchant per liability rules. The cost asymmetry favors lower thresholds (more false positives) since cardholder friction is reversible while fraud loss is often not.
